1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
3	#
4	# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
5	# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
6	# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
7	#
8	#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
9	#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
10	#
11	# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
12	# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
13	# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
14	#
15	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
16	
17	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1
19	
20	# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
21	# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
22	# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
23	# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
24	if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
25	   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
26	   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
28	else
29	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
30	fi
31	
32	_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
33	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
34	
35	# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
36	# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
37	# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
38	# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
39	# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
40	# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
41	# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)
42	
43	# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
45	_orch_not_implemented() {
46	    local fn_name="$1"
47	    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
48	    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
49	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
51	    fi
52	    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
53	    return 1
54	}
55	
56	# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
57	# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.
58	
59	if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
61	fi
62	
63	if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
65	fi
66	
67	if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68	    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
69	    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
70	    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
71	    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
72	    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
73	fi
74	
75	if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
77	fi
78	
79	if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
80	    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
81	fi
82	
83	# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84	# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
85	# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
86	# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
87	orch_has_capability() {
88	    local cap="$1"
89	    local caps
90	    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
91	    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
92	        return 0
93	    fi
94	    return 1
95	}
96	
97	# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
98	# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
99	# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
100	#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
101	#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
102	# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
103	_orch_find_backend_dir() {
104	    local alias="$1"
105	    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"
106	
107	    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1
108	
109	    local manifest plugin_dir
110	    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
111	        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
112	        # Check provides.role
113	        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
114	            continue
115	        fi
116	        # Check id or provides.alias match
117	        local id declared_alias
118	        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
119	        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
120	        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
121	            echo "$plugin_dir"
122	            return 0
123	        fi
124	    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)
125	
126	    return 1
127	}
128	
129	# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130	# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
131	# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
132	# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
133	# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
134	# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
135	orch_load_backend() {
136	    local backend="${1:-}"
137	    local plugin_dir
138	
139	    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
140	        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
141	        return 1
142	    fi
143	
144	    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
145	    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
146	        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
147	        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
148	            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
149	                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
150	                _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
151	                return 1
152	            fi
153	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
154	            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
155	            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
156	            return 0
157	        fi
158	    fi
159	
160	    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
161	    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
162	    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
163	        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
164	            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
165	            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
166	            return 1
167	        fi
168	        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
169	        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
170	        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
171	        return 0
172	    fi
173	
174	    # No plugin found and no fallback — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
175	    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
176	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
177	    return 1
178	}
179	
180	# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
181	# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
182	# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
183	# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
184	_orch_load_backend() {
185	    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
186	    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
187	    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
188	    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
189	    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0
190	
191	    local backend
192	
193	    # Get configured backend, falling back to "sequential" if config unavailable
194	    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
195	        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="sequential"
196	    else
197	        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-sequential}"
198	    fi
199	
200	    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
201	    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
202	    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
203	}
204	
205	# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
206	_orch_load_backend

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true

                return 1
            fi

            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found and no fallback — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
_orch_load_backend() {
    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    local backend

    # Get configured backend, falling back to "sequential" if config unavailable
    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="sequential"
    else
        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-sequential}"
    fi

    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
_orch_load_backend

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/local_engine.sh — shared dispatch/collect/poll/shutdown for the
# local-execution orchestrator backends (orch-bash-parallel, orch-ruflo-hive).
# Extracted from those two plugins in #281 because they had ~80% duplication
# and the #269 normaliser fix had to be applied twice (and still missed
# orch-mock — caught belatedly in #278). Single source of truth now.
#
# Pool layout (caller chooses prefix + pid subdir name):
#   <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/<slot>.pid       — wrapper subshell PID
#   <pool_dir>/results/<slot>.{stdout,stderr,exit,inner_pid}
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ENGINE_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# Defensive source: warn (scripts/lib/helpers.sh).
if ! declare -F warn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
fi
# proc-group.sh supplies zbuild_pg_kill for the process-group kill path (#1801).
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/proc-group.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ORCH_LOCAL_ROOT/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh"

# _orch_local_make_slot_id — collision-resistant slot id (epoch-ns + PID + rand)
_orch_local_make_slot_id() {
    date +%s%N
    printf -- '-%s-' "$$"
    openssl rand -hex 8 2>/dev/null || printf '%05d%05d%05d' $RANDOM $RANDOM $RANDOM
}

# _orch_local_kill_slot <sig> <wrapper_pid> [inner_pid]
# Kills the wrapper's entire process group (TERM then KILL via zbuild_pg_kill)
# so children that ignore TERM are also terminated (#1801, ADR-011 §kill-path).
# The sig argument is accepted for call-site compatibility but zbuild_pg_kill
# handles its own TERM→KILL escalation internally.
_orch_local_kill_slot() {
    local wrapper_pid="$2"
    local inner_pid="${3:-}"
    zbuild_pg_kill "$wrapper_pid"
    [[ -n "$inner_pid" ]] && zbuild_pid_kill "$inner_pid" || true
}

# _orch_local_dispatch_workunit <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <work_unit> <caller_tag>
# Dispatches <work_unit> (must be an executable file path) in a background
# subshell. Records wrapper PID and inner PID; installs trap to propagate
# SIGTERM/EXIT to the inner process.
#
# Output: prints slot_id to stdout AND sets the global _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID.
# Callers needing the slot_id after dispatch (e.g. for downstream telemetry)
# MUST read the global, NOT use command substitution: `$(_orch_local_dispatch_workunit ...)`
# forks a subshell whose EXIT trap (installed by test-helpers.sh or similar)
# `pkill -P $$`s the wrapper subshell we just spawned. The global pattern
# avoids that subshell entirely. (Caught in #282 second-round review.)
#
# Returns 0 on successful dispatch, 1 on validation/permission failure.
_orch_local_dispatch_workunit() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local work_unit="$3"
    local caller_tag="${4:-orch_local}"

    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID=""

    if [[ ! -f "$work_unit" || ! -x "$work_unit" ]]; then
        warn "${caller_tag}: work_unit must be a path to an executable file: ${work_unit}" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Ensure pool dirs exist even if the caller skipped pre-spawn.
    mkdir -p "${pool_dir}/results" "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" 2>/dev/null || {
        warn "${caller_tag}: pool dir is not writable: ${pool_dir}" || true
        return 1
    }

    local slot_id
    slot_id="$(_orch_local_make_slot_id | tr -d '\n')"
    local result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"

    # Background subshell: writes inner work-unit PID, traps on exit to
    # propagate signals, then waits for inner and writes .exit file.
    (
        local rc=0 inner=0
        # #2108: dispatched from a `<<< "$roles_out"` loop — never its stdin.
        bash "$work_unit" </dev/null > "${result_base}.stdout" 2> "${result_base}.stderr" &
        inner=$!
        echo "$inner" > "${result_base}.inner_pid"
        trap 'kill -KILL "$inner" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT INT TERM
        wait "$inner" || rc=$?
        trap - EXIT INT TERM
        echo "$rc" > "${result_base}.exit"
    ) &
    local worker_pid=$!
    echo "$worker_pid" > "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/${slot_id}.pid"
    _ORCH_LOCAL_LAST_SLOT_ID="$slot_id"
    echo "$slot_id"
    return 0
}

# _orch_local_collect_results <pool_dir> <pid_subdir> <timeout_s>
# Polls .exit files for every slot in <pool_dir>/<pid_subdir>/; streams
# stdout/stderr. Returns the normalised orch contract code:
#   0 = all dispatched work units exited 0  (pool dir removed)
#   1 = otherwise (pool dir preserved); _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME says which —
#       `failed` (all exited non-zero) or `partial` (at least one passed).
#       #1850 (ADR-054 §4): `partial` used to be rc 2.
# Work-unit exit codes are normalised — original rc is not passed through.
# Single source of truth for the normaliser (#269 + #278 + #281).
_orch_local_collect_results() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"
    local timeout_s="${3:-0}"
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"

    [[ -d "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}" ]] || { _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"; return 0; }

    local pass_count=0 fail_count=0 timed_out_flag=false
    local deadline=0
    [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 ]] && deadline=$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)} + timeout_s ))

    local pid_file slot_id result_base wrapper_pid inner_pid rc
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        result_base="${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${result_base}.inner_pid" ]] && inner_pid="$(cat "${result_base}.inner_pid")"

        while [[ ! -f "${result_base}.exit" ]]; do
            if [[ "$timeout_s" -gt 0 && "${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date +%s)}" -ge "$deadline" ]]; then
                _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
                echo "124" > "${result_base}.exit"
                timed_out_flag=true
                break
            fi
            sleep 0.1  # fork-budget-exempt: polls until the slot exits — the count is how long it ran (#2236)
        done

        rc="$(cat "${result_base}.exit" 2>/dev/null || echo 1)"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stdout" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stdout"
        [[ -f "${result_base}.stderr" ]] && cat "${result_base}.stderr" >&2
        if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            pass_count=$((pass_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    done

    if [[ "$fail_count" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -rf "$pool_dir"
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="passed"
        return 0
    elif $timed_out_flag; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"
        return 1
    elif [[ "$pass_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="partial"
        return 1
    else
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"
        return 1
    fi
}

# _orch_local_shutdown_pool <pool_dir> <pid_subdir>
# Best-effort SIGTERM → 0.5s → SIGKILL on every slot, then rm -rf the pool dir.
# Idempotent — safe to call on non-existent pools.
_orch_local_shutdown_pool() {
    local pool_dir="$1"
    local pid_subdir="$2"

    [[ -d "$pool_dir" ]] || return 0

    local pid_file slot_id wrapper_pid inner_pid
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot TERM "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    sleep 0.5
    for pid_file in "${pool_dir}/${pid_subdir}/"*.pid; do
        [[ -f "$pid_file" ]] || continue
        slot_id="$(basename "${pid_file%.pid}")"
        wrapper_pid="$(cat "$pid_file")"
        inner_pid=""
        [[ -f "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid" ]] && \
            inner_pid="$(cat "${pool_dir}/results/${slot_id}.inner_pid")"
        _orch_local_kill_slot KILL "$wrapper_pid" "$inner_pid"
    done
    rm -rf "$pool_dir"
    return 0
}

13	# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
16	#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
22	# Collects all results with orch_collect.
23	# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
24	#
25	# Returns:
26	#   0 — all succeeded
27	#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
28	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_fanout() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"

# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
#
# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
# Collects all results with orch_collect.
# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
#
# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
        local collect_rc=0
        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
        orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")" || collect_rc=$?

        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial/timed_out named on
        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "timed_out" ]]; then
            local _fanout_limit; _fanout_limit="$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
            warn "fanout: stage '${stage}' timed out after ${_fanout_limit}s" || true
            _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
            orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
            _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="timed_out"
            return 1
        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        else
            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
        fi
    fi

    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true

    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
    fi
}

# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-timeout-applies-test.sh
#
# SPEC-1 (#1801): A hung work unit dispatched through the fanout, map, or
# sequential strategy stops at its stage template `timeout_s:` limit; the
# 300 s flat deadline no longer applies.
#
# Old code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "${ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300}"
# New code: every strategy calls
#   orch_collect "$pool_id" --timeout "$(template_stage_time_limit "$stage")"
#
# This test fails on old code (spy captures 300), passes on new code
# (spy captures the template's timeout_s: value).
#
# [#1801/SPEC-1]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
# template.sh also sources scripts/lib/stage-time-limit.sh
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/template.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"

print_test_header "orch strategies pass template timeout_s: (not 300s) to orch_collect (#1801 SPEC-1)"
setup_test_env "orch-timeout-applies"

# ── Template with timeout_s: 7 for stage "testjob" ──────────────────────────
# The spy test asserts orch_collect receives --timeout 7, NOT --timeout 300.
TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/tpl-spec1.yaml"
cat > "$TPL" <<'YAML'
id: tpl-spec1
name: spec1 test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout
flow:
  - testjob
testjob:
  roles: [testworker]
  timeout_s: 7
YAML
load_template "$TPL" >/dev/null 2>&1

# Source the strategies (after template.sh so _TPL_SOURCE_FILE is set)
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"

# ── Minimal plugin for resolve_plugin_for_role ───────────────────────────────
_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/testworker"
mkdir -p "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MF'
id: testworker
name: testworker
kind: agent
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: testworker_run
provides:
  role: testworker
MF
cat > "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" <<'PL'
testworker_run() { return 0; }
PL

# Mock orch functions, platform detection, and plugin resolution so the
# strategy machinery runs without a real backend or runner environment.
_DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")
resolve_plugin_for_role() { printf '%s\n' "$_SPEC1_PLUGIN_DIR"; return 0; }

_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_SPEC1_OC_CALLS=0
orch_collect() {
    _SPEC1_OC_CALLS=$(( _SPEC1_OC_CALLS + 1 ))
    _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
    local _s1_pool="$1"; shift
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --timeout) _SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
            *) shift ;;
        esac
    done
    _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
    return 0
}
orch_spawn()    { return 0; }
orch_dispatch() { printf 'slot-%s\n' "$$"; return 0; }
orch_shutdown() { return 0; }

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
printf '{"schema_version":1}' > "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
export ZBUILD_RUN_ID="spec1-test"
export ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/orch-scratch"
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH"
export ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="testjob"

_spec1_expected_timeout="$(template_stage_time_limit testjob)"

# ── SPEC-1a: fanout passes template timeout_s: (not 300) to orch_collect ─────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect"
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1a_rc=0
_strategy_run_fanout "pool-fanout-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi

# With ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 set explicitly, new code must still ignore it
export ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1a2_rc=0
_strategy_run_fanout "pool-fanout-spec1b" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1a2_rc=$?
if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 does not override template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout: template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout}) must win over ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300" \
        "spy got --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true

# ── SPEC-1b: sequential passes template timeout_s: (not 300) to orch_collect ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect"
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1b_rc=0
_strategy_run_sequential "pool-seq-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1b_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"
fi

# With ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 set, sequential must still use template value
export ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1b2_rc=0
_strategy_run_sequential "pool-seq-spec1b" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1b2_rc=$?
if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300 does not override template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] sequential: template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout}) must win over ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT=300" \
        "spy got --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'"
fi
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true

# ── SPEC-1c: map strategy static guard — no longer references ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT ─
# map strategy is too complex to spy on (FIFO pool, sub-pools, batch dispatch),
# but the static guard catches the pattern change at source level.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy no longer uses ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (static guard)"
_MAP_SH="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"
assert_file_exists "SPEC-0: map.sh exists" "$_MAP_SH"
if grep -q 'template_stage_time_limit' "$_MAP_SH"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy calls template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect timeout"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy must call template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect timeout" \
        "not found in $_MAP_SH; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300"
fi
if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_MAP_SH"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy does not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (flat 300 s deadline removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy must not reference ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT (flat 300 s deadline)" \
        "ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT still present in $_MAP_SH"
fi

# ── SPEC-1d: fanout and sequential also have no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT reference ─
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] fanout and sequential source files have no ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT"
for _s1_strat in fanout sequential; do
    _s1_file="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/${_s1_strat}.sh"
    if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT' "$_s1_file"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] ${_s1_strat}.sh: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT removed (flat 300 s deadline gone)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] ${_s1_strat}.sh: ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT must not remain" \
            "still present in $_s1_file; the 300 s flat deadline applies on old code"
    fi
done

# ── SPEC-1 (map runtime spy): map passes template timeout_s: to orch_collect ──
# map.sh uses ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 on old code; must use template_stage_time_limit
# on new code. The spy (defined above) is still the capturing version at this point.
# Fails on old code (spy captures 300); passes on new code (spy captures _spec1_expected_timeout).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-1] map strategy uses template_stage_time_limit for orch_collect (runtime spy)"
unset ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT 2>/dev/null || true
_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT=""
_s1m_rc=0
_strategy_run_map "pool-map-spec1" "testjob" "testworker" \
    "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" \
    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins" 2>/dev/null || _s1m_rc=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT" == "$_spec1_expected_timeout" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: orch_collect received --timeout ${_spec1_expected_timeout} (template timeout_s:, not 300)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-1] map: orch_collect must receive template timeout_s: (${_spec1_expected_timeout})" \
        "spy captured --timeout '${_SPEC1_OC_TIMEOUT:-<none>}'; old code passes ZBUILD_ORCH_TIMEOUT:-300 = 300"

225	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
226	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
227	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
228	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
229	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
230	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
231	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
232	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
233	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
234	    local latest="" n=0 d k
235	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
236	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
237	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
238	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
239	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
240	    done
241	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
242	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
243	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
244	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
245	        return
246	    fi
247	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
248	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
249	}

252	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
253	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
254	_runner_note_push_failure() {
255	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
256	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
257	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
258	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
259	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
260	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"

263	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
264	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
265	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
266	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
267	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
268	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
269	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
270	# reported, never fatal.
271	_runner_push_work_branch() {
272	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
273	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
274	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
275	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
276	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
277	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
278	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
279	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
280	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
281	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
282	    local _err
283	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
284	        return 0
285	    fi
286	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
287	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
288	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
289	    return 0
290	}

292	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
293	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
294	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
295	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
296	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
297	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
298	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
299	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
300	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
301	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
302	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
303	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
304	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
305	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
306	        reattached)
307	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
308	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
309	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
310	        diverged)
311	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
312	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
313	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
314	    esac
315	    return 0
316	}

318	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
319	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
320	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
321	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
322	# never blocks a run.
323	#
324	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
325	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
326	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
327	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
328	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
329	# item 1 of #1807.
330	#
331	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
332	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
333	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
334	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
335	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
336	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
337	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
338	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
339	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
340	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
341	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
342	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
343	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
344	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
345	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
346	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
347	    # push had nothing to send.
348	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
349	
350	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
351	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
352	        saved)
353	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
354	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
355	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
356	            ;;
357	        failed)
358	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
359	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
360	            # no channel to surface on.
361	            #
362	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
363	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
364	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
365	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
366	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
367	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
368	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
370	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
371	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
372	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
373	            fi
374	            ;;
375	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
376	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
377	        *) : ;;
378	    esac
379	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
380	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
381	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
382	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
383	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
384	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
385	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
386	    local _leak=""
387	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
388	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
389	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
390	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
391	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
392	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
393	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
394	        return 0
395	    fi
396	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
397	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
398	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
399	    fi
400	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
401	    return 0
402	}

404	# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
405	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
406	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
407	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
408	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

410	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
411	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
412	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
413	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
414	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
415	_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

417	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
418	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
419	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
420	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
421	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
422	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
423	_runner_now_ms() {
424	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
425	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
426	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
427	        return 0
428	    fi
429	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
430	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
431	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
432	        return 0
433	    fi
434	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
435	}

437	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
438	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
439	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
440	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
441	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
442	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
443	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
444	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
445	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
446	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
447	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
448	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
449	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
450	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
451	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
452	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
453	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
454	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
455	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
456	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
457	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
458	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
459	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
460	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
461	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
462	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
463	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
464	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
465	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
466	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
467	    return 0
468	}

470	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
471	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
472	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
473	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
474	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
475	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
476	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
477	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
478	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
479	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
480	        local i
481	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
482	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
483	            sleep 0.1
484	        done
485	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
486	    fi
487	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    return 0
489	}

491	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
492	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
493	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
494	_runner_now_short() {
495	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
496	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
497	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
498	        return 0
499	    fi
500	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
501	    local out
502	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
503	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
504	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
505	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
506	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
507	    printf '%s' "$out"
508	}

510	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
511	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
512	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
513	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
514	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
515	_runner_duration_token() {
516	    local stage="$1"
517	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
518	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
519	        printf '?s'
520	        return 0
521	    fi
522	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
523	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
524	        printf '?s'
525	        return 0
526	    fi
527	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
528	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
529	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
530	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
531	    else
532	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
533	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
534	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
535	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
536	    fi
537	}

542	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
543	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
544	_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
545	    local state_dir="$1"
546	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
547	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the

553	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
554	    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
555	    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then

560	        fi

573	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
574	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
575	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
576	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
577	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
578	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
579	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
580	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
581	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
582	_runner_record_report() {
583	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
584	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
585	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
586	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
587	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
588	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
589	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
590	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
591	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
592	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
593	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
594	        sleep 0.05
595	    done
596	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
597	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
598	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
599	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
600	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
601	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
602	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
603	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
604	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
605	    else
606	        rm -f "$tmp"
607	    fi
608	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
609	    return 0
610	}

612	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
613	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
614	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
615	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
616	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
617	#
618	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
619	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
620	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
621	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
622	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
623	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
624	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
625	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
626	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
627	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
628	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
629	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
630	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
631	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
632	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
633	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
634	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
635	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
636	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
637	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
638	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
639	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
640	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
645	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
646	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
647	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
648	        return 1
649	    fi
650	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
651	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
652	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
653	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
654	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
655	    #
656	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
657	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
658	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
659	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
660	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
661	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
662	    #
663	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
664	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
665	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
666	    #
667	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
668	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
669	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
670	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
671	    fi
672	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
673	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
674	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
675	    # an unchanged tree.
676	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
677	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
678	    fi
679	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
680	    local _leaf _ok=1
681	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
682	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
683	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
684	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
685	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
686	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
687	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
688	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
689	        esac
690	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
691	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
692	            _ok=0
693	        fi
694	    done
695	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
696	}

698	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
699	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
700	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
701	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
702	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
703	#
704	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
705	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
706	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
707	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
708	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
709	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
710	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
711	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
712	#
713	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
714	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
715	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
716	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
717	#
718	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
719	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
720	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
721	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
722	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
723	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
724	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
725	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
726	_runner_template_personas() {
727	    awk '
728	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
729	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
730	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
731	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
732	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
733	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
734	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
735	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
736	        }
737	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
738	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
739	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
740	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
741	        }
742	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
743	}

745	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
746	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
747	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
748	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
749	    case "$mode" in
750	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
751	        *) mode="warn" ;;
752	    esac
753	
754	    # off = complete no-op, no output
755	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
756	
757	    local -a violations=()
758	    local fail_count=0
759	
760	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
761	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
762	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
763	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
764	    fi
765	
766	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
767	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
768	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
769	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
770	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
771	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
772	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
773	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
774	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
775	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
776	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
777	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
778	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
779	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
780	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
781	    fi
782	
783	    # No violations → clean
784	    [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]] && return 0
785	
786	    # Render all violations in a single block (render-all-at-once pattern).
787	    # #1826 moved the loop itself into _inputs_render_violations so the
788	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
789	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
790	    _inputs_render_violations \
791	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
792	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
793	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
794	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
795	        "${violations[@]}"
796	
797	    # Emit event (best-effort)
798	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
800	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
801	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
802	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
803	    fi
804	
805	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
806	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
807	        return 0
808	    fi
809	
810	    # enforce: fail-closed
811	    return 1
812	}

837	# ─── _runner_pipeline_duration_token (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
838	# Parallel to _runner_duration_token but for the pipeline-wide window. No stage
839	# argument — reads _RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS directly. Returns "?s" on cache
840	# miss so the banner still renders during very-early failures.
841	_runner_pipeline_duration_token() {
842	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"
843	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
844	        printf '?s'
845	        return 0
846	    fi
847	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
848	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
849	        printf '?s'
850	        return 0
851	    fi
852	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
853	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
854	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
855	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
856	    else
857	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
858	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
859	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
860	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
861	    fi

902	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
903	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
904	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
905	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
906	#
907	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
908	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
909	#
910	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
911	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
912	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
913	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
914	#
915	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
916	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
917	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
918	# against banner-write failures.
919	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
920	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
921	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
922	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
923	_runner_restore_stderr() {
924	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
925	    return 0
926	}
